newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese parliament begins voting on 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese parliament begins voting on 1997 budget.

text.p: The Lebanese parliament began voting on Monday on a 1997 budget draft after a five-day debate in which MPs criticised the government inability to keep the deficit on target.
The vote, an article at a time, began at about 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) and might take hours.
The draft, approved by the government in September, sets expenditure at 6,433 billion Lebanese pounds ($4.15 billion) against revenue of 4,100 billion pounds -- a shortfall of 36 percent.

In the debate which began on Wednesday, several deputies questioned the government's ability to meet the proposed deficit target after its failure to do so in previous years. Others warned of ballooning debt.
The 1996 deficit overran a target of 37.6 percent to reach 51 percent. In 1994 and 1995, it exceeded targets of 43 percent and 44 percent respectively, reaching 57 and 47 percent.

The government sees the tight 1997 budget as an attempt to slash Lebanon's massive budget deficits, which are partly caused by heavy spending on Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's multi-billion dollar postwar reconstruction programme.
